result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-024.md for WF02-REQ-024 (/my registrations view with live status, computed waitlist position and the QR pass) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-024, commit e6744a6. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts's new renderCheckInQrPng; apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new getMyRegistrations/MyRegistrationListItem; apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts's new /my command handler; apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts's now-exported STATUS_CATALOG_KEY; apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts's new Catalog.my section; apps/bot/package.json's new qrcode/jsqr/pngjs dependencies) is real user-visible/behavioral surface -- real Telegram messages and photo sends, a real decodable QR image, and a real privacy boundary between users. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3, docs/guides/qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-023.md (reference shape/harness), docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md in full, and the real implementations of renderCheckInQrPng (domain/qr.ts), getMyRegistrations (domain/registration.ts lines 593-650), and handlers/my.ts's full command handler -- plus BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts (pure-function AC3 decode proof) and apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts (AC1 two-user cross-leakage, AC2 capacity-0 direct-withdrawal position recompute, AC3/AC4/AC5 combined four-admission-state fixture) -- so this spec's cases are independently parameterized, not accidental duplicates, and the gap analysis is grounded in what is actually committed.

All 5 stated ACs have at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case, none merely re-pointing at BACKEND-DEV's coverage. Every case uses its own fixtures and its own tg_id range 1000000800+ (distinct from REQ-019/020/021/022/023's own ranges and from handlers/my.test.ts's own internal counter, 950_000_000+, a separate Vitest process).

Gaps closed, case-by-case:
- AC1: BACKEND-DEV's case scans only 5 profile fields (name/company/phone/email) with a 2-user, 1-row-each fixture. This spec's case uses 3 users (a secret user with data spread across TWO registrations -- one admitted, one waitlisted -- plus a third user with ZERO registrations), and scans for all 9 remaining nullable profiles columns (position/isStudent/experienceLevel/linksGithub/linksLinkedin/linksSite/publicBio) plus tgUsername -- 14 identifying needles total, none of which may appear in the viewer's or the zero-registration bystander's captured payloads.
- AC2: BACKEND-DEV's case uses a capacity-0 event where the person ahead withdraws directly from the waitlist -- REQ-023's auto-promotion path is never involved. This spec's case uses capacity-1: the SEAT-HOLDER withdraws, triggering a real REQ-023 auto-promotion of the earliest waitlisted candidate (a materially different code path, promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, than a direct waitlist withdrawal), confirming the viewer's position still recomputes correctly (2 to 1) and their own row's updated_at is byte-identical (toISOString() string equality, not just Date toEqual) before and after.
- AC3: BACKEND-DEV's fixture has exactly one admitted row. This spec's case gives one user TWO admitted registrations across two events with two distinct, non-hand-picked tokens, decoding both photos and confirming each matches its OWN row's token by exact string equality, in the actual returned row order (created_at DESC) -- catching a loop-capture or caching bug a single-row fixture structurally cannot expose.
- AC4: BACKEND-DEV's fixture covers 3 of 5 AdmissionState values (withdrawn/rejected/waitlisted). This spec's case adds the 4th non-admitted value, requested (never exercised in any /my fixture in this codebase), confirming zero photo sends across all four non-admitted rows AND that the requested row's own status label renders correctly (a runtime proof beyond the Record<AdmissionState,...> type's own compile-time exhaustiveness).
- AC5: a static/structural grep of handlers/my.ts confirming exactly one import and one call site of renderCheckInQrPng, zero occurrences of QRCode/the 'qrcode' string literal/the '?start=ci_' template fragment outside domain/qr.ts anywhere in apps/bot/src -- not a dispatch case, per this run's own instruction.

Genuine gap found and closed per this run's explicit instruction to check for it: the empty-registrations case. Confirmed by reading handlers/my.test.ts in full that no existing test dispatches /my for a user with zero registrations, despite handlers/my.ts step 4 having its own distinct code path (rows.length === 0 -> catalog.my.emptyState, return) that is completely unexercised today. Added AC-empty: a fresh user with no registrations gets exactly one sendMessage, exactly the empty-state text, no preceding header, no thrown error. This is the single most likely first-time-user code path (a brand-new bot user with no registrations yet) and was previously untested.

Also added AC-schema (git diff --stat on apps/bot/drizzle, confirmed empty on commit e6744a6, matching the design's explicit no-schema-change claim), AC-deps (grep-based confirmation that qrcode is a runtime dependency while jsqr/pngjs are dev-only decode tooling never imported by production source), and AC-catalog (grep-based parity check of the 3 new Catalog.my keys across types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts), per this project's REQ-020/021/022/023 precedent of covering mechanical claims beyond the numbered ACs.

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement in the spec's own execution-note section, and pointed TEST-RUNNER at REQ-020.md's Shared Setup step 6 for the live-dispatch harness boilerplate and domain/qr.test.ts's own header comment for the jsqr default/callable interop workaround, rather than re-deriving either.

Gap found while reading: none beyond the empty-registrations case this run's own instructions asked to check for, which this spec closes. No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
